about: The standard benchmark suite. Every board runs every test in the classes that apply to it. A test that cannot apply still gets a row (status not_supported or does_not_fit) so the gap shows. Method for each test: docs/methodology.md section 12 and the file in 'method'. Rows live in data/results/*.csv.

classes.setup: Every board: getting from box to a changed program
classes.core: Every MCU: CPU, memory and software stack
classes.analog: Every MCU with an ADC or UART
classes.control: Real-time control loop. Run on C2000, MSPM0 and the wireless parts so the purpose-built chip can be compared
classes.ai: The four room-occupancy models, on CPU, NPU or TMU, plus the vendor's own AI examples
classes.power: Needs a meter (Nordic PPK2 at 3.0 V; TI EnergyTrace at 3.3 V where it runs)
classes.agent: A fresh AI agent doing one job, with and without this repo's docs
classes.sweep: Every vendor example for the board, built and run by script
classes.hobby: The hobby library pack: one driver per part (OLED, TM1637, IR, encoder, motor driver, distance sensors, WS2812) on every MCU board, smallest first
classes.security: Every MCU with 32 kB of RAM or more: post-quantum key exchange and signatures (ML-KEM-768, ML-DSA-44) and the classical operations they replace (ECDSA and ECDH P-256, SHA-256), timed with the CPU's cycle counter after known-answer tests pass. Boards below the RAM floor get does_not_fit rows
classes.host: Radio or sensor parts that have no CPU or too little of one, driven by an external host MCU. Fit (flash and RAM of the host side), then throughput, latency, CPU load and error rate per interface (SPI, UART, I2C), smallest host first. Plan: docs/research/host-scaling-plan-2026-10-09.md
classes.radar: mmWave radar sensors on the bench (IWRL6432BOOST and later radars): time to first frame, detection range and latency, false alarms, UART and SPI data rates, power per update rate. The host-side tests for a radar stream are the `host` class with variants named `radar-*`. Plan: docs/arrivals/iwrl6432boost.md
classes.linux: Linux-class boards (SK-TDA4VM and later): memory latency across the cache levels, scheduling jitter, boot breakdown, storage, cold start of a vision app, inter-core messaging, accelerator and DDR load during inference. Plan: docs/arrivals/tda4.md
classes.motor: One motor and one power stage, control methods compared at equal speed and load: six-step, sine, FOC; Hall, Hall-interpolated, sensorless. Variant <method>-<position>-<point>
classes.motor-bringup: Motor bring-up diagnostics on the bench (driver sense readings, PWM pad sampling, commissioning and six-step trials). Recorded so every bench reading has a row; not a benchmark, compared on no page, and no board is graded on it

tests.name: ML-KEM-768 key generation (FIPS 203)
tests.variants: code, compiler, optimization and memory, e.g. ti-example-ticlang-o2-flash, mlkem-native-gcc-o3-flash
tests.method: one call to keygen from a 64-byte seed, cycles from DWT CYCCNT (M33), SysTick with wrap counter (M0+), esp_cpu_get_cycle_count (RISC-V) or the CPU timer (C28x); median of 3; the image first passes NIST ACVP ML-KEM keyGen test 26 for 768 (the vector TI's pqc_mlkem_768_keygen example carries) and refuses to time otherwise; random seed from the TRNG or a fixed seed, said in conditions

tests.name: ML-KEM-768 encapsulation
tests.method: one call to encaps with a 32-byte seed and a 1,184-byte encapsulation key in RAM; median of 3; known-answer test as keygen plus a cross check that another implementation (TI library, mlkem-native or OpenSSL on the Mac) decapsulates to the same 32-byte secret

tests.name: ML-KEM-768 decapsulation
tests.method: one call to decaps with a 2,400-byte decapsulation key and a 1,088-byte ciphertext; median of 3; must match the encapsulator's secret, and a ciphertext with one bit flipped must give a different secret (implicit rejection)

tests.name: ML-DSA-44 key generation (FIPS 204)
tests.method: one call to keygen from a 32-byte seed; median of 3; the image first passes a NIST ACVP ML-DSA-44 keyGen vector and refuses to time otherwise; seed from the TRNG or fixed, said in conditions

tests.name: ML-DSA-44 sign (FIPS 204), mean over 100 messages
tests.variants: code (ti-example, mldsa-native, mldsa-native-lowram for MLD_CONFIG_REDUCE_RAM), compiler, optimization, memory; pure mode, empty context unless the variant says ctx
tests.method: 100 signs of 100 different 32-byte messages with one key; value is the mean (TI quotes means of 16), value_hi the maximum, median and minimum in the note, because rejection sampling makes sign time vary run to run; deterministic signing (rnd = 0) for the known-answer test (NIST CAVP ML-DSA sign test 1, as in TI's pqc_mldsa_44_sign_ctx_pure), hedged signing for the timed runs, said in conditions

tests.name: ML-DSA-44 verify
tests.method: one verify of a 2,420-byte signature with a 1,312-byte public key; median of 3; must accept NIST CAVP ML-DSA verify test 6 (as in TI's pqc_mldsa_44_verify_ctx_pure) and reject the same signature with one bit flipped

tests.name: Peak stack of one post-quantum call, by painting
tests.variants: operation then code and build, e.g. mlkem768-decaps-mlkem-native-gcc-o3, mldsa44-sign-ti-example-ticlang-o2
tests.method: fill the stack area with a known pattern before the call, scan for the deepest overwritten word after it; excludes the key and message buffers, which the note lists; one row per operation; checked: by-us

tests.name: SHA-256 of 1 kB, cycles per byte
tests.variants: code and build, e.g. ti-cryptolib-sw-ticlang-o2, bcon-sw-ticlang-o2, hw-driver for a SHA block
tests.method: cycles for one-shot SHA-256 of 1,024 bytes in RAM / 1,024; FIPS 180-4 'abc' vector must pass; median of 3

tests.name: ECDSA P-256 sign of a 32-byte digest
tests.variants: code and engine, e.g. ti-example-sw-ticlang-o2 (MSPM0 software), ti-example-pka-ticlang-o2 (MSPM33 PKA), micro-ecc-asm-ticlang-o2, micro-ecc-c-ticlang-o2
tests.method: one sign, median of 3 (best of 3 in the older micro-ecc bench, said in the note); the signature must verify and a one-bit-flipped digest must be rejected; random k from the TRNG or a fixed-seed generator, said in conditions

tests.name: ECDSA P-256 verify
tests.method: one verify, median of 3; must accept a known-good signature (TI's ec_ecdsa_p256_sha256_verify vector where available) and reject a one-bit-flipped one

tests.name: ECDH P-256 shared secret (the classical step ML-KEM replaces)
tests.variants: as ecdsa_p256_sign; x25519 as the code name for the X25519 equivalent
tests.method: one shared-secret computation from our private key and the peer's public key, median of 3; both parties' secrets must match; a full classical join is two of these plus two key generations, which the note adds up beside the ML-KEM-768 total
